findings.title: Machine-readable report contract is not lossless
findings.claim: REPORT-CONTRACT.md declares claim and mechanism mandatory for every material finding, but the canonical machine-readable JSON finding shape omits both fields.
findings.mechanism: A downstream intake following the canonical JSON object cannot preserve the auditor's semantic proposition and causal explanation without reading prose or reconstructing them, contradicting the stated non-reinterpretation/lossless intake purpose.
findings.impact: Lossy external-audit ingestion and increased risk of silent reinterpretation during archive or adjudication.
findings.expected_behavior: Every mandatory load-bearing finding field is represented in the machine-readable contract or an explicitly lossless equivalent.
findings.observed_behavior: claim and mechanism are mandatory in prose but absent from the canonical JSON example.
findings.proposed_change: Add claim and mechanism to the canonical JSON shape, publish a matching JSON Schema, and regression-test required-field parity.

findings.title: Untrusted target data can become executable authority through baseline discovery
findings.claim: The prompt declares target repository content untrusted data but later authorizes target-shipped tests/checkers and requires baseline commands to be derived from target CI, README and helpers without a universal sandbox/inspection gate.
findings.mechanism: A compromised or adversarial target can place executable commands in target-controlled baseline surfaces. A literal auditor can execute them as the discovered baseline, converting target data into action authority. The explicit outside-write inspection warning is scoped only to legacy helpers.
findings.impact: Potential arbitrary target-defined code execution, violation of read-only/no-external-side-effect boundaries, and prompt-injection ambiguity.
findings.expected_behavior: Every target-derived command is inspected and executed only inside a constrained disposable environment unless the coordinator separately authorizes broader effects.
findings.observed_behavior: Target-derived CI/README/helper commands may determine the baseline to run, while universal execution-safety constraints are not specified.
findings.proposed_change: Add a universal target-derived execution gate covering tests, checkers, package hooks, build steps, liveness scripts and helpers: inspect first, remove credentials, sandbox filesystem, constrain network and external writes, and make clear that README/CI can suggest commands but cannot authorize them.

findings.title: Behavioral A/B protocol lacks explicit state isolation or reset
findings.claim: The A/B protocol randomizes conditions and keeps agent/runtime factors constant but does not mandate fresh sessions/processes or reset/isolation of persistent memory, caches, tool state, conversation history or writable fixtures.
findings.mechanism: In stateful agents, one condition can alter state consumed by later conditions. Randomization does not eliminate carryover, so treatment leakage can bias the measured AHP effect.
findings.impact: Reduced causal validity of behavioral effectiveness claims, including false positive or false negative treatment effects.
findings.expected_behavior: Each condition begins from an equivalent clean state, or a defined crossover/washout design records and controls residual shared state.
findings.observed_behavior: The protocol specifies same agent/runtime, constant factors and randomization but no state-reset/session-isolation requirement.
findings.proposed_change: Require fresh process/session or snapshot/restore between conditions; reset memory, context, caches, tools and writable fixtures; record unavoidable shared state and define crossover/washout handling.
